references.text: The consecration of the firstborn is mentioned here for the first time, where the Lord commands that all firstborn be dedicated to Him.
Repeats the command to give the firstborn son and the firstborn of livestock to the Lord.
Everything that opens the womb belongs to the Lord, including the firstborn of cattle and sheep.
Explains that all firstborn belong to the Lord from the day He struck down the firstborn in Egypt.
Detailed rules for redeeming firstborn humans and firstborn of unclean animals, while the firstborn of oxen, sheep, and goats are to be sacrificed.
All male firstborn of cattle and sheep are to be dedicated to the Lord.
The Lord made the Israelites unclean through their offerings when they passed all the firstborn through fire, to show them that He is the Lord.
Refers directly to this law when Jesus, as the firstborn, was brought before the Lord in the temple.
Numbers 18:15 expands on the law of the firstborn by specifying the redemption procedure for humans and unclean animals.
Leviticus 27:26 clarifies that firstborn cannot be dedicated again because they already belong to the Lord.
